basis: Retinal cone degeneration and optic atrophy cause visual impairment; disease is confined to the ocular axis.
Defining microcephaly, microphthalmia and limb defects; oral clefts occur in 80-99%. Cardiac defects are occasional; four-axis cap reached.
Defined by multiple exostoses, brachydactyly and dermal atrophy, each reported in 80-99%.
Developmental delay 2/3; pituitary hypoplasia 1/1; laryngomalacia 1/2. Sparse denominators; less severe limb anomalies omitted at the four-axis cap.
Cutaneous bruising due to capillary fragility; no intrinsic platelet or coagulation defect.
Defined by acute alveolar and pulmonary endothelial injury. Infection is one possible trigger, not an obligatory mechanism.
Carcinoma originates in nasal cavity epithelium; the nasal airway belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Umbrella disorder located in the hypothalamus; endocrine dysfunction varies by subtype and is not established as common across the group.
Defined by cerebellar degeneration, narcolepsy and deafness; optic atrophy reported in 4/4. Diabetes is a separately diagnosed disease.
Neurodevelopmental disease with defining digital anomalies. Central visual impairment is neurologic; swallowing symptoms and separate reflux/apnea do not prove direct organ injury.
Lysosomal storage disease defined by progressive neuronal and retinal degeneration; these features characterize most patients across the group.
Infiltrating facial adipose overgrowth; tongue/parotid involvement and maxillary/mandibular overgrowth each occur in 30-79%. Tonsil enlargement alone does not establish airway injury.
Cerebellar developmental disorder; persistent strabismus occurs in 30-79% and impairs ocular alignment. Dysphagia does not establish intrinsic gastrointestinal injury.
Inherited retinal dysfunction caused by biallelic CNGB3 variants; no established extraocular involvement.
Motor axonal neuropathy; fixed skeletal consequences include hammertoes in 5/5 and Achilles contractures in 2/2, supporting common musculoskeletal impairment.
Non-syndromic congenital absence of an upper limb; no other organ involvement is implied.
Syndromic microphthalmia with intellectual disability; scoliosis, syndactyly and pectus deformity each reported in 4/4. Other visceral defects lack frequency support.
Oocyte and early embryonic maturation failure causes infertility; purely reproductive disease without demonstrated endocrine dysfunction.
Familial motor neuron degeneration with bulbar dysfunction and weakness; these do not establish intrinsic muscle, gastrointestinal or pulmonary disease.
Profound neurodevelopmental disorder; aortic aneurysm reported in 2/5 (40%). Feeding difficulty and incontinence do not establish intrinsic gastrointestinal or renal damage.
The name identifies congenital spinal motor neuron disease; no evidence supports additional organs. Muscle weakness or denervation alone is not intrinsic myopathy.
Optic atrophy 2/6 and esotropia 4/6; contractures 1/3 and pectus deformity 2/6. Respiratory symptoms/infections do not establish direct pulmonary injury.
Defined by cerebral white matter disease and temporal cysts; sensorineural hearing impairment and persistent strabismus each occur in 30-79%.
Peroxisomal metabolic disease defined by demyelination, sensorimotor neuropathy and hearing loss; respiratory weakness does not establish intrinsic lung damage.
Turner phenotype with gonadal failure; congenital cardiac defects ~30-50%, renal malformations ~30%, hearing loss >50% over life. Skeletal abnormalities omitted at the cap.
